native_result.query: How does incarceration affect the wealth of black individuals based on their income levels?
native_result.HypoA: The negative impact of incarceration on wealth for black individuals may be less for the high-income group than those at lower wealth ranges.
native_result.HypoB: Among black respondents in this NLSY79 file, "income level" is not measured - the file contains no income, earnings, wage, poverty, education, occupation or residence field - so income level is proxied here by pre-window asset position (composite_wealth_1985), and on that basis: black men with a jail spell recorded between 1985 and 1994 hold roughly one-fifth the wealth of never-jailed black men by 1996 at every level of baseline assets (ratio of mean 1996 wealth 0.28, 0.30 and 0.16 across the bottom, middle and top 1985 asset strata; a jailed man's wealth ranks below a never-jailed man's 63-71% of the time), so the shortfall is nearly constant in proportional terms across the asset distribution rather than concentrated at one income level - with the shortfall's dollar size rising steeply with baseline position (-$19k to -$27k to -$86k), which is what a constant proportional gap mechanically produces rather than evidence of a steeper hit at the top, and which no formal trend test supports (p_trend >= 0.22) - and the shortfall takes the form of failure to accumulate rather than visible depletion, since jailed medians are flat or negative across 1985-1996 in every stratum (top stratum -$7,038 vs +$12,670, nominal dollars) and remain at or near zero after the jail window closes. This is an unweighted, unadjusted association of jail history with later wealth, stratified on a wealth proxy for income; selection into jail is not controlled, so it should not be read as an effect estimate.
native_result.WorkflowB: 1) Inspected the 6-column file (12,013 rows, 0 missing, no income/earnings/residence field) and confirmed 'income level' is unmeasured. 2) Restricted to race=='black'; inference population = black males (n=1465, 143 jailed); black females descriptive only (16 jailed). 3) Stratified on composite_wealth_1985 into <=0, 1-5000, >5000 (rank/tertile cut degenerate because 37.6% sit at exactly 0); 1990 wealth deliberately excluded from stratifier and covariate role as it lies inside the 1985-1994 jail window. 4) PRIMARY outcome = 1996 wealth level within stratum: medians, means, share with positive wealth, Hodges-Lehmann-free rank measure PS=P(never>jailed)-0.5, sign-preserving log (asinh(x/1000)) difference; 4,000-resample stratified bootstrap percentile CIs; two-sided permutation tests with each statistic centred on its own null (ratio null=1 i.e. tested on the log scale, PS null=0.5, differences null=0); Mann-Whitney and stratified van Elteren rank test; no OLS on raw skewed levels. 5) INTERACTION/TREND: per-stratum gaps in absolute (median, mean) and relative (log ratio of means, log ratio of p75, PS-0.5, gap in share>0) form; cross-stratum slope and heterogeneity tested by permuting jail labels WITHIN stratum (4,000 draws), plus a simulation showing dollar-gap widening is mechanical under a constant proportional gap. 6) SECONDARY: change 1985->1996 (nominal) and ratio-to-baseline so common inflation cancels in the contrast; TERTIARY: 1990 trajectory descriptive only. 7) BASELINE IMBALANCE: within-stratum 1985 jailed/not gaps with permutation tests. 8) SENSITIVITY: exact-duplicate removal reported side-by-side in every table, all-zero-cell removal, and a finer 5-bin stratification. Unweighted sample statistics throughout; associational language only.

sub_hypo.context: Black individuals in the National Longitudinal Study of Youth's 1979 cohort.

gold_sub_hypo.full_hypo: The negative impact of incarceration on wealth for black individuals may be less for the high-income group than those at lower wealth ranges.

sub_hypo.text: Income level is not measured in this NLSY79 file; 1985 composite wealth serves as a proxy for baseline asset position rather than a direct income measure.
sub_hypo.context: Black respondents in the NLSY79 file, which contains no income, earnings, wage, poverty, education, occupation or residence field.
sub_hypo.relations: None; baseline assets proxy unmeasured income level, using strata of <=0, 1–5000 and >5000. Wealth in 1990 is excluded from stratification and covariate roles because it falls within the 1985–1994 jail window.

sub_hypo.text: Black men jailed between 1985 and 1994 have roughly one-fifth the 1996 wealth of never-jailed black men across baseline asset strata, with a nearly constant proportional shortfall rather than a shortfall concentrated at one baseline asset level.
sub_hypo.context: Black male NLSY79 respondents (1,465 men, 143 jailed), stratified by 1985 composite wealth into <=0, 1–5000 and >5000. Estimates are unweighted and unadjusted; selection into jail is not controlled, and the association is not a causal effect estimate.
sub_hypo.relations: Jailed-to-never-jailed mean 1996 wealth ratios are 0.28, 0.30 and 0.16 in the bottom, middle and top baseline asset strata. A jailed man's wealth ranks below a never-jailed man's 63–71% of the time. The proportional shortfall is approximately stable across strata, with no formal trend supported (p_trend >= 0.22).

sub_hypo.text: The dollar shortfall in 1996 wealth associated with jail history rises steeply with baseline assets, but this widening is consistent with a roughly constant proportional gap rather than evidence of a steeper proportional hit at the top.
sub_hypo.context: Black male NLSY79 respondents compared by jail history during 1985–1994 within 1985 wealth strata of <=0, 1–5000 and >5000; unweighted, unadjusted, noncausal comparisons.
sub_hypo.relations: Jailed-minus-never-jailed dollar wealth gaps widen from approximately -$19,000 to -$27,000 to -$86,000 across increasing baseline asset strata. Dollar-gap widening is mechanically compatible with a constant proportional gap; formal trend tests do not support a steeper proportional shortfall at higher baseline assets (p_trend >= 0.22).

sub_hypo.text: The later wealth shortfall among jailed black men takes the form of failure to accumulate rather than visible depletion: median wealth trajectories are flat or negative across 1985–1996 in every baseline asset stratum and remain at or near zero after the jail window closes.
sub_hypo.context: Black male NLSY79 respondents, stratified by 1985 wealth into <=0, 1–5000 and >5000 and compared by jail history during 1985–1994. Changes are nominal and unweighted; 1990 trajectories are descriptive only, and comparisons do not control selection into jail.
sub_hypo.relations: Jailed men's median wealth changes over 1985–1996 are flat or negative in every stratum, with post-window wealth at or near zero. In the top baseline asset stratum, the nominal median change is -$7,038 for jailed men versus +$12,670 for never-jailed men, consistent with an accumulation shortfall.
